package_info.package_name: Mercedes Me Connect / SiriusXM Connected Vehicle Services (infrastructure and apps)
package_info.package_versions: Not specified; all versions using the vulnerable SSO and cloud infrastructure
package_info.why_malicious: The infrastructure and applications exposed sensitive internal development environments, source code, and cloud resources due to authentication and access control flaws. This allowed unauthorized access to mission-critical systems, source code, and sensitive data, creating a high risk of supply chain compromise, remote code execution, and privilege escalation.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Public registration page for repair shops writes to the same database as the core employee LDAP system, allowing non-employees to create accounts with broad internal access.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During user registration, the application writes new user data to the central LDAP directory, granting access to internal SSO-protected resources, including source code repositories and internal tools.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Non-employees can register and gain access to internal systems intended for employees only.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict internal access to verified employees; here, external users can escalate privileges.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate repair shops may need limited access, but not to internal development or source code systems.
key_indicators: Public registration writes to employee LDAP
No separation between external and internal user privileges

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Newly created user credentials from the public registration portal allow login to internal GitHub repositories containing sensitive source code and documentation.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After registration, the user logs in via SSO and gains access to internal GitHub repositories, exposing source code and internal documentation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: External users should not have access to internal source code repositories.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Source code repositories are expected to be restricted to vetted developers; here, any registered user can access them.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only internal developers should have this access.
key_indicators: SSO grants access to internal code repositories
No access control separation between internal and external users

execution_context.file_location: Internal cloud deployment services, Jenkins, AWS control panels

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SSO credentials allow access to cloud deployment panels, Jenkins, AWS, and internal APIs, enabling remote code execution and management of internal systems.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After SSO login, the user can access cloud management interfaces, request/manage internal systems, and execute code on internal infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: External users can perform administrative actions on critical infrastructure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Only trusted, authenticated employees should have access to cloud and CI/CD management panels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this level of access is highly privileged.
key_indicators: SSO tokens grant cloud admin access
No privilege separation or additional verification

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: JavaScript bundles contain hardcoded API endpoints and sensitive credentials/constants, exposing backend API routes and sometimes credentials.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime or during reverse engineering, the code reveals backend API endpoints and sensitive constants, enabling attackers to target backend systems directly.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sensitive credentials and internal API routes should not be exposed in client-side code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Production client code should not contain secrets or internal endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: API endpoints may be exposed, but not credentials.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Leaked AWS keys provide full organizational read/write access to S3 buckets, exposing user databases, source code, and config files.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: With compromised AWS keys, an attacker can list, read, and modify all files in S3 buckets, exfiltrating sensitive data and potentially modifying production assets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Full S3 access allows exfiltration and tampering with critical data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: AWS keys should be tightly controlled and never exposed.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only trusted cloud admins should have this access.

attack_chain.action: Register a new user via the public Mercedes repair shop portal, writing to the central LDAP directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Obtain SSO credentials with internal access

attack_chain.action: Use SSO credentials to access internal GitHub repositories and source code.
Leverage SSO credentials to access cloud deployment panels, Jenkins, AWS, and internal APIs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and infrastructure control

attack_chain.action: Extract sensitive API endpoints and credentials from JavaScript bundles.
attack_chain.leads_to: Direct backend API attacks and further data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Use leaked AWS keys to access and exfiltrate all files from SiriusXM S3 buckets.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of user databases, source code, and configs

behavioral_signatures: External user registration leading to internal SSO access
Unusual access to internal GitHub or cloud panels from non-employee accounts
Access to sensitive source code or documentation by newly created accounts
Extraction of hardcoded credentials from client-side JavaScript
Unusual S3 bucket access patterns or mass downloads
file_indicators: Public registration portals writing to employee LDAP
JavaScript bundles with hardcoded credentials or internal API endpoints
AWS keys present in source code or config files
network_indicators: SSO login attempts from external IPs to internal resources
API calls to internal endpoints from unauthorized accounts
Large data transfers from S3 buckets to unfamiliar destinations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new user registrations that gain access to internal SSO-protected resources. Alert on access to source code repositories, cloud management panels, or sensitive documentation by accounts not previously seen. Scan client-side code for hardcoded credentials or internal API endpoints. Audit AWS key usage for anomalous access patterns, especially mass downloads or access from new locations.
